findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without an enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 default. Sensitive report data would be unprotected at rest under customer-controlled keys.

No ACL is specified and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy restricting public access, leaving the bucket's exposure dependent on account-level defaults and vulnerable to accidental public ACL/policy grants.
No logging block is configured, so access to this bucket and its objects is not recorded to the audit_trail bucket, preventing detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised data access.
Object versioning is not enabled, so objects can be silently overwritten or deleted by an attacker with write access with no recoverable prior version (no MFA-delete protection either).
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial ledger data is stored without an enforced default encryption key.
No logging block is defined for this bucket holding ledger exports, so reads and writes are not captured in the audit_trail bucket.
Versioning is not enabled on the ledger bucket, leaving sensitive financial exports vulnerable to irreversible overwrite or deletion.
The bucket relies only on a private ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a later policy or ACL change could expose ledger data publicly without a hard guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored without enforced default server-side encryption.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guarding this bucket; the private ACL alone does not prevent a future public bucket policy or object ACL grant.

The runbooks bucket has no default server-side encryption configured; operational runbooks frequently contain internal procedures, hostnames, and credentials material and are stored unencrypted under customer-managed keys.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbooks is not audited to the audit_trail bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is attached, leaving the bucket without an account/bucket-level guardrail against public ACLs or policies.
The audit log destination bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL but has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; audit logs are high-value evidence and should be hard-blocked from public exposure.
The audit trail bucket does not log access to itself (or another bucket), so tampering with or exfiltration of audit logs would leave no trace.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing supplier PII/contract data) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so it is stored without customer-controlled encryption.
